open_questions.question: Do 17-point covering sets with split (11,6)/(6,11) exist? The two surviving sharp rows are (e_ex, b_ex, c) = (5,1,1) and (6,0,1), each with shared = 1 and A_x = B_x = 1 at the unique shared sum.
open_questions.why_it_matters: It decides the last open family of PR 2542's 'No 17-point set covers F2^7' claim and therefore whether |P| = 17 is possible at all for a universal word (at L = 22 the split (11,6) is parity-feasible).
open_questions.first_step: A k = 11 budget-5/6 census of the same raw {0,3} domain (resumable per sub-shard; the completed budget-4 walk took 54 minutes) demotes the rows one by one; surviving rows need a row-restricted joint search: enumerate 11-sets of E with the row's excess and collision shape and for each run a constrained B-side DFS (6-sets of the odd coset) forced to cover E \ {0} \ supp(A) with the exact shared-sum and cross-coverage constraints.
open_questions.blocked_by: The B side has ~3.1e8 Sidon 6/7-sets and cannot be enumerated outright; the joint tree needs orbit reduction (GL(6,2) invariance is proved here and fixes 0, 3 in A, but stabilizer canonical forms for the pair (A,B) are not implemented).

open_questions.question: Is r((C2)^7) = 20, i.e. do 18-point or 19-point covers of F2^7 exist (PR 2542 open question 2, sharpened by PR 2634)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It settles the set-level restricted addition basis value and bounds |P| from below for universal words at L = 20 and L = 22.
open_questions.first_step: Extend this package's sharp-row machinery to k = 18/19 (the collision-multiplicity identity applies unchanged) and run the same min-excess census per split row.
open_questions.blocked_by: The same joint-tree growth; the exact census here covers the 17-point rows only.
